findings.title: Rapid7 Analysis: VMware vCenter SRP Authentication Bypass to Root (CVE-2026-123890)
findings.summary: Overview An unauthenticated attacker can retrieve the session key for an in-progress administrator login to VMware vCenter's directory service. The attacker then uses that key to complete the login without knowing the account's password. The vulnerable interface is exposed through DCE/RPC on TCP port 2012. The issue, tracked as CVE-2026-123890 , combines a Secure Remote Password (SRP) session-key getter that is callable before authentication with an RPC context lookup that does not enforce ownership. The context handles use predictable UUIDv1 values. By creating two reference contexts around a pending login, an attacker can narrow the hidden login handle to a short timestamp window and ask the server for its key. We reproduced the bypass against vCenter Server Appliance 8.0.2.00400, build 23929136 , running Photon OS 4.0, and leveraged the resulting administrator connection through to root command execution. SSH and Bash access were initially disabled. The attack recovered the directory database and its Security Token Service (STS) signing key, forged an administrator API session, and used appliance administration features to create an account and enable SSH. Neither the existing SSO password nor the root password was an input to that chain. Impact The attacker needs network access to TCP 2012 and the name of an existing SSO principal. Our PoC uses the default SSO administrator principal, administrator@vsphere.local ; deployments using a different SSO domain need the corresponding account name. The attack does not depend on an existing authenticated connection or an administrator being online. The attacker initiates the login attempt in order to recover its session key. The authenticated connection can call the directory database-copy interface. Its raw database contains the STS private signing key, allowing the attacker to sign administrator assertions that vCenter trusts. findings.title: AVideo API vulnerable to OS command injection through an unescaped FFmpeg process keyword
secp256k1-native has a compiler-induced timing side channel in scalar multiplication
findings.summary:
## Summary

`Point#mul` — the default, constant-time scalar multiplication and the library's headline secret-scalar operation — could leak timing information about the secret scalar (a private key or ECDSA-style nonce in a downstream consumer) **not because of a source-level bug, but because the compiler reconstructed a branch from branchless source.**

The Montgomery ladder selects between point candidates with `uint256_select`, written deliberately branchlessly as `r = (a & ~mask) | (b & mask)` with a mask that is all-ones or all-zeros. GCC 15.2 at `-O2` recognises this select idiom, reconstructs the original boolean condition, and emits a secret-dependent conditional jump (`je`/`jne`). The branch's taken/not-taken timing correlates with the secret scalar bits flowing through the ladder.

This silently undid the 0.17.0 fix for the historical |t|=875 infinity-branch leak, which had relied on `uint256_select` compiling to branchless code.

## Impact

A timing side-channel on the secret scalar in constant-time scalar multiplication. For a consumer that calls `Point#mul` (or the native `scalar_multiply_ct`) on a secret key or nonce and exposes timing to an attacker (e.g. an online signing oracle), repeated measurements can statistically recover scalar bits — the classic ECC private-key/nonce timing-attack setting (cf. Brumley–Boneh). The leak is in the *compiled binary*; the source is correct, so source review and the deterministic ctgrind check on a *non-reconstructing* toolchain do not reveal it.

Pre-1.0 with no published RubyGems dependents, so this is handled as fix-publish-and-document: full GHSA + CVE record without a coordinated downstream-notification timeline. The CVE is filed for citability so the empirical record (paper → review → compiler regression → fix) is permanent and searchable.

findings.title: Vulnerability in Oracle OpenJDK (Java4Shell) Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 17, 2026, Oracle announced the availability of fixes for a vulnerability in OpenJDK that could lead to remote code execution identified by CVE-2026-114938. The vulnerability affects OpenJDK Java 17.0.6 and later on x86-64 platforms when processing Base64 encoded content. For more information, see the Oracle Critical Security Patch Update Advisory - November 2026 and the OpenJDK Vulnerability Advisory: 2026/11/17 . For additional information, see the Talos blog post: Talos Threat Advisory CVE-2026-114938: Critical vulnerability in OpenJDK JAVA This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nov2026-java-rce-eCa6ss9z Security Impact Rating: High CVE: CVE-2026-114938

findings.title: Vulnerability in PHP Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 19, 2026, the PHP Foundation announced the availability of security fixes that address a critical vulnerability that could lead to remote code execution. This vulnerability is identified by CVE-2026-126714. For information about this vulnerability, see the advisory GHSA-fm2m-fjf5-v3cp . This vulnerability is being referenced as phpAfterShell . For information about Splunk products and offerings, see Vulnerabilities in PHP affecting Splunk Products - November 2026 . This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-phpaftershell-nov-2026-kT9pL4Xe Security Impact Rating: Critical CVE: CVE-2026-126714

findings.title: Vulnerabilities in nginx Affecting Cisco Products: November 2026
findings.summary: On November 18, 2026, nginx announced the availability of a fix for multiple critical vulnerabilities in nginx that could lead to remote code execution. These vulnerabilities affect nginx releases 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 and is fixed in releases 1.31.9 (mainline) and 1.30.7 (stable). These vulnerabilities were identified by the following CVEs: CVE-2026-113425: NGINX ngx_mail_proxy_module vulnerability CVE-2026-121810: NGINX ngx_http_v3_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123007: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123633: NGINX ngx_http_v2_module vulnerability CVE-2026-123634: NGINX resolver vulnerability For more information, see the nginx Security Advisories . This advisory will be updated as additional information becomes available. This advisory is available at the following link: https://sec.cloudapps.cisco.com/security/center/content/CiscoSecurityAdvisory/cisco-sa-nginx-nov-2026-e8jska2s Security Impact Rating: High CVE: CVE-2026-113425,CVE-2026-121810,CVE-2026-123007,CVE-2026-123633,CVE-2026-123634
